name: Rotary
description: A Leslie cabinet: a horn and a bass drum that spin at their own speeds, heard through two microphones, with the slow run-up between chorale and tremolo.

params.name: Speed
params.description: Slow is the gentle chorale, Fast the tremolo. The horn changes speed quickly and the drum lags behind. Brake lets both coast to a stop.

params.name: Horn Depth
params.description: How strongly the spinning horn moves the highs, in pitch, level and brightness. At zero the highs stand still.

params.name: Drum Depth
params.description: How strongly the spinning drum moves the lows, mostly in level with a little pitch wobble. At zero the lows stand still.

params.name: Acceleration
params.description: How quickly the rotors speed up and slow down when Speed changes. Low is a heavy, slow run-up; high gets there almost at once.

params.name: Drive
params.description: Overdrive from the tube amplifier ahead of the rotors. Zero is clean. Higher settings add growl and even out the level.

params.name: Balance
params.description: Level of the horn against the bass drum. Low settings favour the lows from the drum; high settings favour the highs from the horn.

params.name: Distance
params.description: How far the microphones are from the cabinet. Close pulses strongly as the horn passes; far is smoother and more chorused.

params.name: Spread
params.description: The angle between the two microphones. At zero both hear the same and the cabinet is mono; higher settings widen the movement.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the dry signal and the cabinet. The cabinet hears the input summed to mono.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. The speeds, crossover and run-up times are those of a Leslie 122 in outline; the cabinet is a geometric sketch (path length, facing and a few reflections per microphone), not a measured model.
